A1.justification: Both ten-page PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. All pages were compared; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original multi-label classification experiments on MIMIC and MS-COCO, with results in Tables 2–4 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains the original MIMIC and MS-COCO experiments and their results in Tables 2–4 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: The proposed loss in Equation 13, similarity and dissimilarity factors in Equations 14–15, positive-sample definitions, and training procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six MIMIC settings: MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV ICD-9/ICD-10 under full and top-50 label coverage. Both also evaluate MS-COCO image classification.

E2.justification: ALL, ANY, and MulSupCon remain the evaluated comparison losses throughout the corresponding MIMIC and MS-COCO experiments. No comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Table 1 retain identical splits, metrics, encoder configurations, preprocessing, and stopping procedures, including batch sizes of 128 for MIMIC and 64 for MS-COCO.

E4.justification: The illustrative relation case in Section 2.4.1 and analyses accompanying the ICD-9 and top-50 evaluations are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity test, robustness test, or error analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 and Figure 2 contain identical results. For example, Table 4 retains the proposed method's MS-COCO scores of 65.3 Macro-F1, 70.2 Micro-F1, and 92.8 Precision@1.

T1.justification: The five label-set relation definitions, Equations 1–19, and Propositions 1–4 with their accompanying reasoning and proofs are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about five sample–anchor relations, the proposed loss, and its effectiveness across encoders and datasets. The revised title does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Both retain the limitations concerning supervised-only applicability, batch size, augmentation, and the lack of specific treatment of label co-occurrence and long-tailed distributions.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 retains identical optimizer, scheduling, augmentation, input-length, and early-stopping details. Dataset-version and access disclosures are also unchanged; no reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the references are identical, including the positioning relative to MulSupCon, earlier supervised contrastive learning, and loss-reweighting approaches.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Similarity-Dissimilarity Loss with Supervised Contrastive Learning for Multi-label Classification' to 'Similarity-Dissimilarity Loss for Multi-label Supervised Contrastive Learning'. Affiliation-marker spacing and the arXiv version/date stamp also change. Body prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–4 retain identical formatting, captions, and placement. Pages 2–10 are pixel-identical, and the revised title occupies the existing two-line title block without changing the page layout.

improvement.justification: The revision rephrases the title and updates front matter while retaining identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, and limitations. These limited editorial changes do not produce a meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
